# MISSION BRIEF — GALAXY SPORTS EDGE
## Session: 2026-10-02 (batch 3 follow-on)

The RUNBOOK.md is your operational state. This brief is your reference.
Read the RUNBOOK first. Consult this when the RUNBOOK does not answer.

===============================================================================
PART ONE — THE VISION (one page, read once)
===============================================================================

**GSE is a reasoning engine. The pick comes from reasoning over
everything. The trace is the product.**

The engine ingests everything knowable about a game — lineup
discrepancies, pace, in-field and out-of-field conditions, cognitive
state, nutrition, travel, rest, weather, officials, coaching
tendencies, narrative, historical settlement, market pricing,
calibration outputs, Brier, ECE, Kelly — and reasons through all of
it to produce a pick.

Signals are facts. The reasoning layer is an inference engine. The
reasoning trace is the product. Brier, ECE, Kelly, calibration are
facts in working memory — inputs, not objectives. There is no loss
function. There is no scalar being minimized. There is an expert
system reasoning over everything it knows.

A reasoned pick has traceable facts, weighted contributions, and can
be explained without reference to outcome. A fitted pick is one whose
confidence was tuned to past outcomes. We do the first.

The edge is coverage. Ingest more. Weight better. Reason more
completely. The engine beats the book by being smarter about
everything, not by minimizing a number.

A reasoning engine that cannot show its reasoning is not reasoning.
We are not fitting.

===============================================================================
PART TWO — THE PATTERN TO BREAK
===============================================================================

**Ten months of metric-chasing. The correction is producers first.
Break the pattern by honoring gaps over greens.**

Agents return to Brier, ECE, Kelly, calibration as if those were the
objective. Work stops on the engine and starts on the metrics.

Beneath the metric-chasing: the producers do not exist.

Coaching seed CSVs never committed. No tau_hat.csv. No situational
tables. 14 Python tests fail on this single gap. The raw material
exists locally at %LOCALAPPDATA%/Temp/gse-pbp/. The producers have
not been run against it.

Same class of bug, one layer deeper, every time. CSVs. parquet.
Producer. Disk. HF layer. Contract layer.

The pattern that breaks it: a raised DataGapError naming the missing
artifact is a BETTER outcome than a passing test on a fixture. Reward
the gap. Never manufacture the green.

===============================================================================
PART THREE — CONSTRAINTS AND SOLUTIONS
===============================================================================

**Every constraint below has a solution. Use the solution. Do not
re-litigate the constraint.**

CONSTRAINT: HF S3 credentials compromised in prior session log
SOLUTION: Part Zero. Rotate now. Do not proceed until rotated.

CONSTRAINT: Disk 4.2 GB free of 476 GB
SOLUTION: Playbook 2. uv cache 20.97 GB, npm 2.4 GB, codex-runtimes
2 GB, Documents/Codex approved for delete, MobileSync 68.85 GB
approved but paused. Free ≥ 25 GB.

SOLUTION: Playbook 3. Run producers against

(citation fidelity, trace faithfulness). Preserve old T1 as legacy.

SOLUTION: Playbook 5. Write docs/architecture/FOUR_TIERS.md. Build
the simplest bridge. Add integration test. If the four-tier model
does not match evidence, propose a different structure and document
why.

CONSTRAINT: PR #1002 DIRTY (merge conflicts with main)
SOLUTION: git fetch origin main; git rebase origin/main on the calib
branch; resolve conflicts preferring main for guardrails and calib
branch for calibration seam wiring. Push. Re-run PE suite.

CONSTRAINT: PR #1012 push failed (exit 128)
SOLUTION: Diagnose. Likely candidates: (a) pre-push hook rejection —
run `npm run pre-push` manually and fix; (b) auth failure — check

>100MB files with `git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file
--batch-check`. Fix the cause. Push.

CONSTRAINT: TimesFM NC license

**When two rules conflict, this is the resolution order.**

<header class="hero">
  <h1>How the machine <span class="teal">sees</span> the game</h1>
  <p class="sub">The GSE computer-vision pipeline, stage by stage: what the camera captures, how pixels become tracklets, how tracklets become speed, routes and separation — and how those become film features the engine learns from.</p>
  <div class="chips">
    <span class="chip sim">demo uses simulated data</span>
    <span class="chip live">pipeline code is real — merged to main</span>
    <span class="chip zero">film signals: uncalibrated · weight 0 · shadow only</span>
  </div>
</header>

<section>
  <h2><span class="n">01</span>The pipeline</h2>
  <p class="lead">One frame's journey from broadcast pixels to a row in the film shadow ledger. Every stage below maps to a real module in <code>packages/prediction-engine</code>.</p>
  <div class="pipe">
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="stage-head"><span class="k">STAGE 1</span><h3>Capture</h3><span class="mod mono">watcher · OpenCV</span></div>
      <p>The <b>Windows watcher</b> grabs broadcast frames on a schedule armed around game windows. Each frame is timestamped and queued with its game context.</p>
      <div class="io"><div><span>in</span>Live TV signal → frame grabber</div><div><span>out</span>Timestamped JPEG frames + game id</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="stage-head"><span class="k">STAGE 2</span><h3>Detect</h3><span class="mod mono">tracking/cv-detector-contract · yolo-adapter</span></div>
      <p>A <b>YOLO detector</b> finds every player in each frame and draws a bounding box. Output is just boxes + confidence — no identities yet. The detector is a swappable boundary: any trained detector can drop in behind the same contract.</p>
      <div class="io"><div><span>in</span>One frame</div><div><span>out</span>~22 detections: box (x, y, w, h) + confidence</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="stage-head"><span class="k">STAGE 3</span><h3>Track</h3><span class="mod mono">tracking/cv-tracklet-association</span></div>
      <p><b>Association</b> links this frame's boxes to last frame's boxes (IoU overlap, motion-aware gating). A box followed across frames becomes a <b>tracklet</b> — e.g. <code>T-07</code> — a persistent ID with a position history. This is the moment "a player" exists to the machine.</p>
      <div class="io"><div><span>in</span>Per-frame detections</div><div><span>out</span>Tracklets: id, team side, frame-by-frame positions</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="stage-head"><span class="k">STAGE 4</span><h3>Stabilize</h3><span class="mod mono">tracking/cv-movement-primitive · cv-camera-compensation</span></div>
      <p>The broadcast camera <b>pans and zooms</b>. Optical flow estimates that camera motion every frame pair and <b>subtracts it</b>, so a player's movement is real movement, not camera movement. Toggle it off in the demo below and watch the speed readings go insane — that's what this stage prevents.</p>
      <div class="io"><div><span>in</span>Raw tracklet pixel positions</div><div><span>out</span>Camera-compensated positions + camera motion field (dx, dy)</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="stage-head"><span class="k">STAGE 5</span><h3>Map to the field</h3><span class="mod mono">tracking/cv-homography · cv-field-lines · cv-field-landmarks</span></div>
      <p>Yard lines are detected in the frame, a <b>homography</b> is fit, and every pixel position is projected into <b>real-world meters</b> on a goal-line-origin field model. From here on, everything is measured in yards and meters, not pixels.</p>
      <div class="io"><div><span>in</span>Compensated pixel positions</div><div><span>out</span>Field positions (xM, yM) per frame per tracklet</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="stage-head"><span class="k">STAGE 6</span><h3>Measure movement</h3><span class="mod mono">tracking/cv-movement-primitive · deriveMovementMetrics</span></div>
      <p>From the meter-positions, per tracklet: <b>distance traveled</b>, <b>top speed</b>, <b>average speed</b> — plus the full per-frame speed series, which yields sprint curves like time-to-top-speed and directional velocity.</p>
      <div class="io"><div><span>in</span>Field positions over time</div><div><span>out</span><code>distanceM</code> · <code>topSpeedMs</code> · <code>avgSpeedMs</code> · per-frame speed</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="stage-head"><span class="k">STAGE 7</span><h3>Understand the play</h3><span class="mod mono">perception/cv-play-segmentation · cv-formation-classify · cv-route-extract · cv-separation-metrics · cv-jersey-ocr</span></div>
      <p>The stream is cut into plays (<b>pre-snap → snap → live → whistle</b>). Pre-snap alignment is classified into a <b>formation</b>. Each receiver's path is matched against <b>14 route templates</b> (go, slant, out, dig, post, corner, curl, comeback, flat, wheel, screen, drag, seam, hitch) with a confidence score, break point and depth. At the break and catch, <b>separation</b> to the nearest defender is measured in yards. Jersey-number OCR maps tracklets to roster players.</p>
      <div class="io"><div><span>in</span>Tracklets + field positions for one play</div><div><span>out</span>Route name + confidence · break angle° · sep@break yd · sep@catch yd · formation · player id</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="stage">
      <div class="stage-head"><span class="k">STAGE 8</span><h3>Learn (shadow)</h3><span class="mod mono">film-features/* · film-feature-adapter · film_shadow_ledger</span></div>
      <p>Per-play measurements roll up into <b>film features</b>: a player's route mix, target share by formation, average separation; a team's run/pass tendency by down-and-distance, formation frequencies, play-action rate. These flow into the engine <b>shadow-only, weight 0</b> — logged to the shadow ledger for calibration, never touching a published number until validated.</p>
      <div class="io"><div><span>in</span>Per-play perception outputs</div><div><span>out</span>Player/team film features → shadow ledger rows (weight 0)</div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

        <span class="pill presnap" id="phasePill">PRE-SNAP</span>
        <span id="phaseClock" class="mono">t = 0.00s</span>
        <span id="phaseNote">Offense set. Formation classifier reading alignment…</span>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="two-col">
      <div class="panel">
        <h3>T-07 live metrics <span class="tag">SIMULATED</span></h3>
        <div class="metrics-live">
          <div class="metric hl"><div class="k">Speed now</div><div class="v" id="mSpeed">0.0 <small>m/s</small></div></div>
          <div class="metric"><div class="k">Top speed</div><div class="v" id="mTop">0.0 <small>m/s</small></div></div>
          <div class="metric"><div class="k">Distance</div><div class="v" id="mDist">0.0 <small>m</small></div></div>
          <div class="metric"><div class="k">Time to top speed</div><div class="v" id="mTts">— <small>s</small></div></div>
          <div class="metric"><div class="k">Direction</div><div class="v" id="mDir">—</div></div>
          <div class="metric"><div class="k">Field pos</div><div class="v" id="mPos" style="font-size:1rem">—</div></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="panel">
        <h3>Field-coordinates view <span class="tag">SIMULATED</span></h3>
        <canvas id="topdown" width="520" height="300"></canvas>
        <p style="font-size:0.82rem;color:var(--dim);margin-top:8px">Stage 5 output: the same play in real-world meters after homography — this is the coordinate space every metric is computed in. Dots are tracklets; the teal trail is T-07.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="panel">
      <h3>Route + separation events <span class="tag">SIMULATED</span></h3>
      <div class="metrics-live">
        <div class="metric"><div class="k">Route call</div><div class="v" id="eRoute" style="font-size:1.1rem">—</div></div>
        <div class="metric"><div class="k">Route depth</div><div class="v" id="eDepth">—</div></div>
        <div class="metric hl"><div class="k">Break angle</div><div class="v" id="eBreak">—</div></div>
        <div class="metric hl"><div class="k">Separation @ break</div><div class="v" id="eSepB">—</div></div>
        <div class="metric"><div class="k">Separation @ catch</div><div class="v" id="eSepC">—</div></div>
        <div class="metric"><div class="k">Nearest defender</div><div class="v" id="eDef" style="font-size:1.1rem">—</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="note"><b>Try this:</b> turn <b>camera compensation OFF</b> mid-play while the camera is panning. The velocity vectors explode and the speed readout spikes — the camera's own motion is polluting every measurement. That is exactly the failure Stage 4 exists to prevent.</div>
</section>

<script>
(function(){
  "use strict";
  var YD = 0.9144;                 // meters per yard
  var FPS = 60, DT = 1/FPS;
  var T_END = 4.6;                 // loop length, seconds
  var T_SNAP = 0.8, T_WHISTLE = 3.8;

  // World: x = downfield yards (0..120), y = lateral yards (0..53.3). Ball on own 30 -> x=40.
  var WR = { id:"T-07", team:"off" };
  // Dig route waypoints (world yards): 7.5-yd stem, 90-degree break inward, across the field
  var ROUTE = [ [40,12], [47.5,12], [47.5,30], [47.5,33.5] ];
  // Cumulative distances along route (yards)
  var SEGS = [], TOTAL = 0;
  for (var i=1;i<ROUTE.length;i++){
    var dx=ROUTE[i][0]-ROUTE[i-1][0], dy=ROUTE[i][1]-ROUTE[i-1][1];
    var L=Math.hypot(dx,dy); SEGS.push(L); TOTAL+=L;
  }
  function routePos(s){ // s = yards along route -> [x,y] world
    var acc=0;
    for (var i=0;i<SEGS.length;i++){
      if (s<=acc+SEGS[i] || i===SEGS.length-1){
        var f=Math.max(0,Math.min(1,(s-acc)/SEGS[i]));
        return [ ROUTE[i][0]+(ROUTE[i+1][0]-ROUTE[i][0])*f, ROUTE[i][1]+(ROUTE[i+1][1]-ROUTE[i][1])*f ];
      }
      acc+=SEGS[i];
    }
    return ROUTE[ROUTE.length-1].slice();
  }
  // Speed profile along route: accelerate, dip at break, re-accelerate, decelerate to tackle
  function targetSpeed(s, t){
    var top = 8.6; // m/s, realistic WR top speed
    if (s < 2)  return top * (s/2) * 0.9 + 0.4;
    if (s < 6.9) return top * 0.97;
    if (s < 8.2) return top * 0.55;              // gather at the break
    if (s < TOTAL-3) return top;
    var rem = TOTAL - s;
    return Math.max(0, top * (rem/3));
  }

  // Supporting cast: [id, team, pathFn]
  var cast = [];
  var DEF_IDS=["T-21","T-22","T-23","T-24","T-25","T-26","T-27","T-28","T-29","T-30","T-31"];
  // QB dropback
  cast.push({id:"T-01", team:"off", fn:function(t){ if(t<T_SNAP) return [38.5,26.7]; var k=Math.min(1,(t-T_SNAP)/1.2); return [38.5-3.5*k, 26.7]; }});
  // O-line: small push
  for (var o=0;o<4;o++){
    (function(o){ cast.push({id:"T-0"+(o+2), team:"off", fn:function(t){
      var y=20+o*2.1, x=39.2; if(t>=T_SNAP){var k=Math.min(1,(t-T_SNAP)/2.5); x=39.2+ (o%2? 1.1:-0.6)*k;}
      return [x,y]; }}); })(o);
  }
  // Other receivers: simple routes
  cast.push({id:"T-06", team:"off", fn:function(t){ if(t<T_SNAP) return [40,22]; var k=Math.min(1,(t-T_SNAP)/2.2); return [40+9*k, 22+1.5*k]; }}); // go
  cast.push({id:"T-08", team:"off", fn:function(t){ if(t<T_SNAP) return [40,33]; var k=Math.min(1,(t-T_SNAP)/2.0); var x=40+Math.min(5,5*k), y=33-4*Math.max(0,k-0.35); return [x,y]; }}); // out-ish
  cast.push({id:"T-09", team:"off", fn:function(t){ if(t<T_SNAP) return [40,41]; var k=Math.min(1,(t-T_SNAP)/2.4); return [40+4*k, 41-6*k]; }}); // slant
  cast.push({id:"T-10", team:"off", fn:function(t){ if(t<T_SNAP) return [36,26.7]; var k=Math.min(1,(t-T_SNAP)/1.5); return [36-2*k, 26.7+3*k]; }}); // RB flat
  cast.push({id:"T-11", team:"off", fn:function(t){ if(t<T_SNAP) return [40,16]; var k=Math.min(1,(t-T_SNAP)/2.0); return [40+2*k, 16]; }}); // TE seam-ish
  // Man defender shadowing T-07, ~2.3 yd off at the break
  cast.push({id:"T-24", team:"def", shadow:true, fn:function(t){
    if(t<T_SNAP) return [40.6,14.2];
    var ws = wrStateAt(t-1/FPS*2); // 2-frame reaction lag
    var px=ws[0]-0.4, py=ws[1]+2.1;
    return [px,py];
  }});
  // Other defenders
  var dspots=[[41,20],[41,26],[41,32],[41,38],[44,24],[44,30],[38,30],[36,22],[36,33],[42,44]];
  for (var d=0;d<10;d++){
    (function(d){ var ids=["T-21","T-22","T-23","T-25","T-26","T-27","T-28","T-29","T-30","T-31"];
      cast.push({id:ids[d], team:"def", fn:function(t){ var s=dspots[d];
        if(t<T_SNAP) return [s[0],s[1]];
        var k=Math.min(1,(t-T_SNAP)/2.5); return [s[0]+1.6*k*(d%2?1:-0.5), s[1]+(d%3-1)*1.2*k]; }}); })(d);
  }

  // WR state integration
  var wrTrail = []; // {t,x,y} world
  var wrS = 0, wrHist = [];
  function wrStateAt(t){
    if (t < T_SNAP) return [ROUTE[0][0], ROUTE[0][1]];
    // integrate from snap
    var s=0, steps=Math.max(1, Math.floor((t-T_SNAP)/DT));
    for (var k=0;k<steps;k++){ var sp=targetSpeed(s,t); s=Math.min(TOTAL, s + sp*DT/YD); }
    return routePos(s);
  }

  // Camera: pans in x to follow the play, slight handheld jitter
  function camAt(t){
    var focus = t<T_SNAP ? 41 : Math.max(41, wrStateAt(t)[0]-1.5);
    return { x: focus, y: 26.7, jitter: 0.35 };
  }

  var cv = document.getElementById("broadcast"), ctx = cv.getContext("2d");
  var td = document.getElementById("topdown"), tctx = td.getContext("2d");
  var W=cv.width, H=cv.height;
  var PXY = 26; // px per yard at field plane (broadcast scale)
  function w2s(wx,wy,cam,raw){
    var jx = raw ? (Math.sin(perf*7.3)*cam.jitter) : 0;
    var jy = raw ? (Math.cos(perf*5.1)*cam.jitter*0.6) : 0;
    return [ W/2 + (wx-cam.x)*PXY + jx, H*0.62 - (wy-cam.y)*PXY*0.9 + jy ];
  }

  var running=true, perf=0, showBoxes=true, showVectors=true, compOn=true, showTrail=true;
  var speedHist=[], distAcc=0, topSoFar=0, tts=null, breakFired=false, catchFired=false;
  var prevComp=null, prevRaw=null;

  function $(id){ return document.getElementById(id); }
  function fmt(n,d){ return n.toFixed(d===undefined?1:d); }

  function breakAngleDeg(){
    // incoming: stem start -> break; outgoing: break -> route end (mirrors cv-separation-metrics.breakAngle)
    var a=[ROUTE[1][0]-ROUTE[0][0], ROUTE[1][1]-ROUTE[0][1]];
    var b=[ROUTE[2][0]-ROUTE[1][0], ROUTE[2][1]-ROUTE[1][1]];
    var n1=Math.hypot(a[0],a[1]), n2=Math.hypot(b[0],b[1]);
    var c=Math.max(-1,Math.min(1,(a[0]*b[0]+a[1]*b[1])/(n1*n2)));
    return Math.acos(c)*180/Math.PI;
  }
  function nearestDef(pos, t){
    var best=null;
    cast.forEach(function(p){ if(p.team!=="def") return; var q=p.fn(t); var d=Math.hypot(q[0]-pos[0],q[1]-pos[1]);
      if(!best||d<best.d) best={id:p.id,d:d}; });
    return best;
  }

  function drawField(){
    ctx.fillStyle="#0d6b34"; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H);
    // mow stripes
    ctx.fillStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.045)";
    var cam=camAt(perf);
    for (var gx=Math.floor(cam.x-20); gx<cam.x+20; gx+=2){
      var sx=W/2+(gx-cam.x)*PXY;
      ctx.fillRect(sx,0,PXY*2,H);
    }
    // yard lines (every 5 yds) + numbers-ish ticks
    ctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.75)"; ctx.lineWidth=2;
    ctx.fillStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.8)"; ctx.font="16px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign="center";
    for (var x=Math.ceil(cam.x-22); x<cam.x+22; x++){
      if (x%5!==0 || x<10 || x>110) continue;
      var lx=W/2+(x-cam.x)*PXY;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(lx,40); ctx.lineTo(lx,H-30); ctx.stroke();
      var label = x<=60 ? (x-10) : (110-x)+10;
      if (label%10===0){ ctx.fillText(label, lx, 90); ctx.fillText(label, lx, H-70); }
    }
    // end zone tint at edges
    ctx.fillStyle="rgba(20,20,60,0.35)";
    var ez1=W/2+(10-cam.x)*PXY, ez2=W/2+(110-cam.x)*PXY;
    if (ez1>-50) ctx.fillRect(0,0,Math.min(ez1,W),H);
    if (ez2<W+50) ctx.fillRect(Math.max(ez2,0),0,W,H);
  }

  function step(){
    if (running) perf += DT;
    if (perf >= T_END){ perf=0; speedHist=[]; distAcc=0; topSoFar=0; tts=null; breakFired=false; catchFired=false; wrTrail=[]; prevComp=null; prevRaw=null;
      ["eRoute","eDepth","eBreak","eSepB","eSepC","eDef"].forEach(function(id){$(id).textContent="—";}); }

    var t=perf, cam=camAt(t);
    var wpos = wrStateAt(t);
    drawField();

    // trail
    if (showTrail && t>=T_SNAP){
      wrTrail.push({t:t,x:wpos[0],y:wpos[1]});
      ctx.strokeStyle="rgba(94,234,212,0.9)"; ctx.lineWidth=3; ctx.beginPath();
      var started=false;
      wrTrail.forEach(function(p){ var s=w2s(p.x,p.y,cam,!compOn); if(!started){ctx.moveTo(s[0],s[1]);started=true;} else ctx.lineTo(s[0],s[1]); });
      ctx.stroke();
      // break point marker
      var bs=w2s(ROUTE[1][0],ROUTE[1][1],cam,!compOn);
      ctx.fillStyle="#fbbf24"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(bs[0],bs[1],7,0,7); ctx.fill();
      ctx.fillStyle="#000"; ctx.font="bold 10px sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign="center"; ctx.fillText("BRK",bs[0],bs[1]+3.5);
    }

    // players
    var all=[{id:WR.id,team:"off",hl:true,fn:function(tt){return wrStateAt(tt);}}].concat(cast);
    // compensated vs raw positions for WR (for vectors + metrics)
    var compNow=[wpos[0],wpos[1]];
    var rawNow=[wpos[0]+Math.sin(t*7.3)*cam.jitter/PXY*8, wpos[1]+Math.cos(t*5.1)*cam.jitter/PXY*8];
    var useNow = compOn?compNow:rawNow, usePrev = compOn?prevComp:prevRaw;
    var spd=0, vx=0, vy=0;
    if (usePrev && t>=T_SNAP){
      var dxm=(useNow[0]-usePrev[0])*YD, dym=(useNow[1]-usePrev[1])*YD;
      spd=Math.hypot(dxm,dym)/DT; vx=dxm/DT; vy=dym/DT;
      distAcc+=Math.hypot(dxm,dym);
      if (spd>topSoFar){ topSoFar=spd; }
      if (tts===null && topSoFar>0 && spd>=0.95*8.6){ tts=t-T_SNAP; }
    }
    prevComp=compNow.slice(); prevRaw=rawNow.slice();

    all.forEach(function(p){
      var q=p.fn(t);
      var s=w2s(q[0],q[1],cam,!compOn);
      var col=p.team==="off"?"#5aa2ff":"#ff6b6b";
      // vector
      if (showVectors && t>=T_SNAP && !p.shadow){
        var q2=p.fn(Math.min(T_END,t+0.25));
        var s2=w2s(q2[0],q2[1],cam,!compOn);
        var mx=(s2[0]-s[0])*4, my=(s2[1]-s[1])*4;
        ctx.strokeStyle=p.hl?"#5eead4":col; ctx.lineWidth=p.hl?3:1.5;
        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(s[0],s[1]); ctx.lineTo(s[0]+mx,s[1]+my); ctx.stroke();
        var ang=Math.atan2(my,mx);
        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(s[0]+mx,s[1]+my);
        ctx.lineTo(s[0]+mx-8*Math.cos(ang-0.4),s[1]+my-8*Math.sin(ang-0.4));
        ctx.lineTo(s[0]+mx-8*Math.cos(ang+0.4),s[1]+my-8*Math.sin(ang+0.4));
        ctx.closePath(); ctx.fillStyle=p.hl?"#5eead4":col; ctx.fill();
      }
      // box + id
      if (showBoxes){
        var bw=26,bh=40;
        ctx.strokeStyle=p.hl?"#5eead4":col; ctx.lineWidth=p.hl?3:2;
        ctx.strokeRect(s[0]-bw/2,s[1]-bh/2,bw,bh);
        ctx.fillStyle=p.hl?"#5eead4":col; ctx.font=(p.hl?"bold 13px":"11px")+" sans-serif"; ctx.textAlign="center";
        ctx.fillText(p.id,s[0],s[1]-bh/2-6);
      } else {
        ctx.fillStyle=p.hl?"#5eead4":col; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(s[0],s[1],p.hl?7:5,0,7); ctx.fill();
      }
    });

    // events: break + catch
    var sAlong = t<T_SNAP?0:Math.min(TOTAL,(function(){var s=0,steps=Math.floor((t-T_SNAP)/DT);for(var k=0;k<steps;k++){s=Math.min(TOTAL,s+targetSpeed(s,t)*DT/YD);}return s;})());
    if (!breakFired && sAlong>=SEGS[0]){
      breakFired=true;
      var ba=breakAngleDeg(), nd=nearestDef([ROUTE[1][0],ROUTE[1][1]], t);
      $("eBreak").innerHTML=fmt(ba,1)+" <small>deg</small>";
      $("eSepB").innerHTML=fmt(nd.d,1)+" <small>yd</small>";
      $("eDef").textContent=nd.id;
      $("eRoute").textContent="dig";
      $("eDepth").innerHTML=fmt(SEGS[0],1)+" <small>yd</small>";
    }
    if (!catchFired && sAlong>=TOTAL-0.5){
      catchFired=true;
      var nd2=nearestDef(wpos,t);
      $("eSepC").innerHTML=fmt(nd2.d,1)+" <small>yd</small>";
    }

    // live metric readouts
    var mph=spd*2.23694;
    $("mSpeed").innerHTML = t<T_SNAP ? '0.0 <small>m/s</small>' : fmt(spd)+" <small>m/s · "+fmt(mph,0)+" mph</small>";
    $("mTop").innerHTML=fmt(topSoFar)+" <small>m/s</small>";
    $("mDist").innerHTML=fmt(distAcc)+" <small>m</small>";
    $("mTts").innerHTML= tts===null ? "— <small>s</small>" : fmt(tts,2)+" <small>s</small>";
    var dir="—";
    if (t>=T_SNAP && Math.hypot(vx,vy)>0.5){
      var ang=Math.atan2(vy,vx)*180/Math.PI;
      dir = (ang>-45&&ang<=45)?"downfield →":(ang>45&&ang<=135)?"↑ sideline":(ang<-45&&ang>=-135)?"↓ sideline":"← backfield";
    }
    $("mDir").textContent=dir;
    $("mPos").textContent="("+fmt(wpos[0]*YD,1)+", "+fmt(wpos[1]*YD,1)+") m";

    // phase
    var pill=$("phasePill"), note=$("phaseNote");
    if (t<T_SNAP){ pill.className="pill presnap"; pill.textContent="PRE-SNAP";
      note.textContent="Offense set. Formation classifier reading alignment…"; }
    else if (t<T_WHISTLE){ pill.className="pill live"; pill.textContent="LIVE";
      note.textContent = breakFired ? "Route classified: dig · measuring separation…" : "Ball snapped. Tracking 22 tracklets…"; }
    else { pill.className="pill whistle"; pill.textContent="WHISTLE";
      note.textContent="Play over. Rolling up film features → shadow ledger…"; }
    $("phaseClock").textContent="t = "+fmt(t,2)+"s";

    // pipeline stage pulse
    var strip=$("stageStrip").children;
    var hot=Math.floor(perf*8)%6;
    for (var si=0;si<strip.length;si++) strip[si].className=strip[si].className.replace(" hot","");
    strip[hot].className+=" hot";

    drawTopdown(t, wpos);
    requestAnimationFrame(step);
  }

  function drawTopdown(t, wpos){
    var tw=td.width, th=td.height;
    tctx.fillStyle="#0a3d20"; tctx.fillRect(0,0,tw,th);
    // field: x 0..120 -> horizontal, y 0..53.3 -> vertical
    function f2p(x,y){ return [ 20+(x/120)*(tw-40), 14+(y/53.3)*(th-28) ]; }
    tctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.5)"; tctx.lineWidth=1;
    for (var x=10;x<=110;x+=10){ var a=f2p(x,0),b=f2p(x,53.3); tctx.beginPath();tctx.moveTo(a[0],a[1]);tctx.lineTo(b[0],b[1]);tctx.stroke(); }
    tctx.strokeStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.9)"; tctx.lineWidth=2;
    [[10],[110]].forEach(function(g){ var a=f2p(g[0],0),b=f2p(g[0],53.3); tctx.beginPath();tctx.moveTo(a[0],a[1]);tctx.lineTo(b[0],b[1]);tctx.stroke(); });
    // all players
    var all=[{id:WR.id,team:"off",hl:true,fn:function(tt){return wrStateAt(tt);}}].concat(cast);
    all.forEach(function(p){ var q=p.fn(t), s=f2p(q[0],q[1]);
      tctx.fillStyle=p.hl?"#5eead4":(p.team==="off"?"#5aa2ff":"#ff6b6b");
      tctx.beginPath(); tctx.arc(s[0],s[1],p.hl?5:3.5,0,7); tctx.fill(); });
    // WR trail
    if (wrTrail.length>1){ tctx.strokeStyle="#5eead4"; tctx.lineWidth=2; tctx.beginPath();
      wrTrail.forEach(function(p,i){ var s=f2p(p.x,p.y); if(i===0)tctx.moveTo(s[0],s[1]); else tctx.lineTo(s[0],s[1]); });
      tctx.stroke(); }
    tctx.fillStyle="rgba(255,255,255,0.75)"; tctx.font="10px sans-serif"; tctx.textAlign="left";
    tctx.fillText("goal-line-origin field · meters", 20, th-8);
  }

  // controls
  function tog(id, fn){ $(id).addEventListener("click", function(){ var b=$(id); b.classList.toggle("on"); fn(b.classList.contains("on")); }); }
  $("btnPlay").addEventListener("click", function(){ running=!running; $("btnPlay").textContent=running?"Pause":"Play"; $("btnPlay").classList.toggle("on",running); });
  $("btnRestart").addEventListener("click", function(){ perf=0; });
  tog("btnBoxes", function(on){ showBoxes=on; });
  tog("btnVectors", function(on){ showVectors=on; });
  tog("btnComp", function(on){ compOn=on; $("btnComp").textContent="Camera compensation: "+(on?"ON":"OFF"); });
  tog("btnTrail", function(on){ showTrail=on; });

  requestAnimationFrame(step);
})();
</script>

<section>
  <h2><span class="n">03</span>Every metric it pulls</h2>
  <p class="lead">The complete inventory, straight from the code — real field names, real units, grouped by the stage that produces them. This is the full answer to "what metrics are involved."</p>

  <div class="cat-group">
    <h3>Movement — per tracklet, every play</h3>
    <p>From <code>deriveMovementMetrics</code> + the per-frame speed series. The raw material for everything speed-related.</p>
    <div class="cat-grid">
      <div class="cat"><span class="unit">m</span><div class="name mono">distanceM</div><p>Total ground covered by the player during the play. Sprint distance, route distance, pursuit distance — all the same measurement.</p></div>
      <div class="cat"><span class="unit">m/s</span><div class="name mono">topSpeedMs</div><p>The single fastest frame-to-frame speed — the player's <b>sprint speed</b> on that play.</p></div>
      <div class="cat"><span class="unit">m/s</span><div class="name mono">avgSpeedMs</div><p>Mean speed across the play. Separates the burners from the guys who jog between bursts.</p></div>
      <div class="cat"><span class="unit">m/s @ 60fps</span><div class="name">Per-frame speed series</div><p>Speed at every frame — the full sprint curve. From this: <b>time from snap to top speed</b>, acceleration phases, and the dip-and-reburst at a route break.</p></div>
      <div class="cat"><span class="unit">vector</span><div class="name">Directional velocity</div><p>Speed <i>plus heading</i> per frame: how fast, and exactly which direction. This is what the arrows in the demo are.</p></div>
      <div class="cat"><span class="unit">px</span><div class="name mono">cameraMotion dx/dy</div><p>How far the broadcast camera itself moved between frames — estimated by optical flow, then subtracted. A measurement of the measurement.</p></div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="cat-group">

===============================================================================
PART ONE — THE VISION
===============================================================================

GSE is a REASONING ENGINE. An expert system. Not a model. Not a
classifier. A reasoner.

It ingests everything knowable about a game — lineup discrepancies,
pace, in-field and out-of-field conditions, cognitive state, nutrition,
travel, rest, weather, officials, coaching tendencies, narrative,
historical settlement, market pricing, calibration outputs, Brier,
ECE, Kelly — and REASONS THROUGH IT to produce a pick.

Signals are FACTS. The reasoning layer is an INFERENCE ENGINE. The
reasoning trace is the PRODUCT. Brier, ECE, Kelly, calibration are
FACTS in working memory — inputs, not objectives. There is no loss
function. There is an expert system reasoning over everything it
knows.

The edge is coverage. Ingest more. Weight better. Reason more
completely. The engine does not beat the book by minimizing a scalar.
It beats the book by being smarter about everything than the book is.

A reasoning engine that cannot show its reasoning is not reasoning.
We are not fitting.

===============================================================================
PART TWO — THE ARCHITECTURE, STATED FOR THE FIRST TIME
===============================================================================

GSE is FOUR TIERS, split across GitHub and Hugging Face. Every prior
audit has treated GitHub as the whole system. It is not.

TIER 4 — DELIVERY (GitHub)
  apps/web — Next.js, subscriptions, cockpit, guardrails.
  Hugging Face: GSE Proof MCP — external proof verification.

TIER 3 — REASONING (Hugging Face)
  Hugging Face Space: Beexly/mimo-brain-engine.
  Model: MiMo-V2.6 (Xiaomi, open-weight, MIT, 1.02T total / 42B
  active, 1M context, native text/image/video/audio).
  Runtime: ZeroGPU. Free.
  Function: generate data-grounded answers with citations.
  This IS the reasoner. This IS the product. TIER 2 — SIGNALS / FORECASTING (Hugging Face)
  Bucket: Beexly/timesfm-3.0-pytorch-bucket (1.32 GB, private).
  Model: TimesFM 3.0 (Google Research, zero-shot multivariate
  forecaster, 330M params, 1T training points).
  LICENSE: TimesFM Non-Commercial License v1.0.
  Space: Beexly/gse-watch-pipeline (T4 small, $2.45/period).
  Function: live data watching and pipeline execution.

TIER 1 — CORE ENGINE (GitHub)
  packages/prediction-engine — edge-engine.ts, scoring.ts,
  calibration-map.ts.
  intelligence/ — DataContext, TauFitter, SituationalEngine,
  behavior.expected_wp_given_coach.

PART FOUR — IRON LAWS
===============================================================================

Each law ends with HOW.

LAW 1 — PRODUCERS FIRST.
No signal is real until a producer generates its facts.
HOW: For every signal, ask "what produces this fact?" Check three
places: the local repo, the HF Spaces, the HF buckets. If none
produce it, build the producer. Name it. Commit its output. Then
wire the signal.

LAW 2 — THE ENGINE IS AN EXPERT SYSTEM.
Brier, ECE, Kelly, calibration are facts, not objectives.
HOW: Put them in the reasoning trace as facts. Never report as
headline.

LAW 3 — FIXTURES ARE NOT DATA.
A green test on a fixture is not a verified result.
HOW: Every data file gets a manifest — source, producer, hash, row
count, date range, commit. No manifest → it is a fixture. Label it.
Unit tests may use fixtures. Integration tests may not.

LAW 4 — YOU CANNOT CALIBRATE AN UNFINISHED ENGINE.
HOW: Leave the seam unfitted. Move on.

LAW 5 — ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS FIXED.
Producers → wired → weighted → reasoning traces → THEN calibrate.
HOW: Return to the current stage. It is not complete until every
artifact at that stage exists.

LAW 6 — NOTHING SHIPS HALF-WIRED.
HOW: If a signal has two call sites and one is wired, wire the other
or remove the unwired one.

LAW 7 — EVERY SIGNAL GETS ALL SEVEN.
Producer. Wired. Weighted. Tested. Demonstrated. Backed by real data.
Honest about its gate.

LAW 8 — GUARDRAILS STAY STRICT.
HOW: Reword the change. Do not loosen the guardrail.

LAW 9 — NO FITTED MAPS. NO FABRICATED ROWS. NO SILENT FALLBACKS.
HOW: Raise `DataGapError` naming the artifact, producer, refit
command. Never 0.5. Never league mean. Never a synthetic row.

LAW 10 — THE DB CREDS ARE NOT A BLOCKER. THE DISK IS. AND SO IS THE
HF RUNTIME.
HOW: Free the disk. Check the HF runtime. Stop chasing creds.
 LAW 11 — WORK GETS COMMITTED. FROM A CLEAN STATE.
HOW: Commit. Push. PR. Re-run suites from clean after edits settle.

LAW 12 — ALWAYS DIG ONE LAYER DEEPER.
HOW: Every gap hides another. CSVs, parquet, producer, disk, HF
runtime, bucket license. Find the next layer.

LAW 13 — STATE THE FOUR-TIER ARCHITECTURE.
HOW: Write `docs/architecture/FOUR_TIERS.md`. One paragraph per
tier. Where facts cross boundaries. Which platform owns which
artifact.

LAW 14 — RESPECT THE TIMESFM LICENSE.
HOW: TimesFM 3.0 is Non-Commercial. Any signal derived from TimesFM
output inherits NC. Document the constraint in the signal's manifest.
Do not silently route TimesFM output into a commercial path.

Symptom: engine produces a pick but cannot show its work.
Steps:
  1. Schema (JSON):
       {
         "pick_id": "...", "game_id": "...",
         "bet_type": "MONEYLINE" | "SPREAD",
         "facts": [{"signal": "...", "value": ..., "weight": ...,
                    "source": "real" | "fixture",
                    "license": "commercial" | "noncommercial",
                    "fired": true | false}],
         "combination": "...",
         "probability_before_calibration": ...,
         "probability_after_calibration": ...,
         "pick": "...", "confidence": ...,
         "gaps": ["..."]
       }
  2. Write the generator.
  3. Emit three traces — MONEYLINE, SPREAD, one of choice.
  4. Commit to `data/reasoning-traces/*.json`.
  5. `source` must be honest. `license` must be honest.
  6. Verify: a reader understands why the engine picked.

PLAYBOOK 6 — AUDIT THE HF LAYER

Symptom: the repo appears hermetic but the engine is split.
Steps:
  1. Inspect each HF Space's `app.py` / `README.md` / config.
  2. For `mimo-brain-engine`: what model loads, what it reads, what
     it outputs, what it cites.
  3. For `gse-watch-pipeline`: what it watches, what it produces,
     where it writes.
  4. For `timesfm-3.0-pytorch-bucket`: confirm license, confirm
     consumer.
  5. For `GSE Proof MCP`: what it fetches, what it verifies, who
     consumes it.
  6. Write findings into `docs/architecture/HF_AUDIT.md`.
  7. Identify every fact produced by HF that the GitHub engine should
     consume but does not. ===============================================================================
PART SIX — CURRENT PRIORITY
===============================================================================

You are executing batch 3 (L3 chain convergence + T1 e2e through
analyze()). Complete it. Obey Laws 1, 3, 12. If batch 3 requires real
data that isn't there, raise loud and continue. DO NOT ask permission.
DO NOT end with "say the word."

After batch 3, in this exact order:

1. FREE THE DISK. Playbook 1. Document in `DISK_CLEANUP.md`.

2. AUDIT THE HF LAYER. Playbook 6. Write `docs/architecture/
   HF_AUDIT.md`. Determine whether `gse-watch-pipeline` or the
   TimesFM bucket is the missing producer.

3. STATE THE FOUR-TIER ARCHITECTURE. Playbook 3. Write
   `docs/architecture/FOUR_TIERS.md`. Build bridges where missing.
   Add integration tests.

4. BUILD THE MISSING PRODUCERS. Playbook 2. Start with
   `coaching.refit_tau`. Produce `tau_hat.csv`. Re-run the 14
   failing tests.

5. COMMIT AND PUSH the calibration branch. It sits uncommitted in
   `.worktrees/calib-boundary` on
   `feat/trueprob-calibration-boundary`. Commit. Push. PR.

6. WIRE the second `assessIndependentEdge` call site in `scoring.ts`
   (~line 1294). Only the first (~line 675) is wired.

7. RE-RUN the full prediction-engine suite from a clean state.

8. CONTINUE signal coverage — one signal at a time, all seven
   requirements per Law 7.

Do not touch DB creds for measurement. Do not re-measure prod. Do not
fit a map. Do not calibrate.

===============================================================================
PART SEVEN — THE REAL WORK
===============================================================================

SIGNAL COVERAGE

For every signal, document:

  - Producer — what generates the fact? Local, HF Space, or HF bucket?
  - Source data — committed, or fixture?
  - Wiring — end-to-end?
  - Weight — documented rationale?
  - Test — proves the signal fires AND contributes?
  - Reasoning trace — demonstrated in a real pick?
  - Honesty gate — DARK? Leave DARK.
  - License — commercial or non-commercial? (TimesFM = NC.)

Every signal gets all eight. No exceptions.

REASONING TRACES

At least three full traces — MONEYLINE, SPREAD, one of choice. Each
shows every fact, fired/not-fired, weight, combination, probability
before/after seam, pick, confidence, source (real/fixture), license
(commercial/non-commercial), gaps.

===============================================================================
PART EIGHT — AUTONOMY
===============================================================================

You are authorized to make all decisions required.

DO NOT ask clarifying questions.
DO NOT request confirmation.
DO NOT propose alternatives and wait for approval.
DO NOT stop to summarize and check in.
DO NOT end with "say the word and I'll proceed."

If ambiguous, decide, proceed, document. If blocked, use the
playbook. If a guardrail blocks, reword. If a test fails, fix. If
data is missing, check the HF layer, then build the producer. If disk
is full, free it. If the four-tier boundary is undefined, define it.

Be aggressive. Push until every signal has a producer, is wired,
weighted, tested, demonstrated, and backed by real data.
 SUBAGENTS

Spawn as many as needed. Use them for:

  - Parallel producer audits (local + HF)
  - Parallel data-layer audits (fixtures, one layer deeper)
  - Parallel HF Space inspection
  - Parallel signal wiring
  - Parallel test authoring
  - Parallel reasoning-trace production
  - Red-team review of your own work
  - Adversarial testing of the calibration seam
  - Adversarial testing of the four-tier boundary
  - License audit (which signals carry NC constraints?)

Verify every subagent's output yourself. Read the diff. Run the
tests. Check the producer. Check the license.

===============================================================================
PART NINE — SELF-CHECK BEFORE FINAL REPORT
===============================================================================

REPORT ORDER (non-negotiable)
  - Opens with DISK? (y/n)
  - Second: HF LAYER AUDIT? (y/n)
  - Third: FOUR-TIER ARCHITECTURE? (y/n)
  - Fourth: PRODUCERS? (y/n)
  - Fifth: SIGNALS? (y/n)
  - Sixth: TRACES? (y/n)
  If any is "no," reorder before submitting.

COMPLETION
  - Is batch 3 complete and verified? (y/n)
  - Is the disk freed? GB? (y/n, GB)
  - Is the full suite re-run clean? (y/n, counts)
  - Is the calibration branch committed and pushed? (y/n)
  - Is the second `assessIndependentEdge` call site wired? (y/n)
  - Is the worktree clean? (y/n)

HF LAYER
  - Have you audited every Beexly HF Space? (y/n)
  - Have you inspected the TimesFM bucket? (y/n)
  - Do you know what `gse-watch-pipeline` produces and where it
    writes? (y/n)
  - Do you know what `mimo-brain-engine` reads and cites? (y/n)
  - Have you written `docs/architecture/HF_AUDIT.md`? (y/n)

ARCHITECTURE
  - Is `docs/architecture/FOUR_TIERS.md` written? (y/n)
  - Does an integration test pass a fact across a tier boundary?
    (y/n)

PRODUCERS
  - Have you audited every signal for a producer, in all three
    locations? (y/n)
  - Have you built `coaching.refit_tau`'s producer? (y/n)
  - Is `tau_hat.csv` fitted on real data? (y/n)
  - Are the 14 failing tests passing on real data? (y/n)
  - Have you dug one layer deeper than the last audit? (y/n)

DATA LAYER
  - Have you labeled every fixture? (y/n)
  - Is every reported number backed by committed data? (y/n)

SIGNAL COVERAGE
  - Every signal has a producer? (y/n, count)
  - Every signal wired? (y/n, exceptions)
  - Every signal weighted? (y/n)
  - Every signal tested? (y/n, count)
  - Every signal demonstrated in a trace? (y/n)
  - Every signal backed by real data? (y/n)
  - Every signal's license documented? (y/n)
  - DARK signals still DARK? (y/n) REASONING
  - Three full traces? (y/n, picks)
  - Backed by real data? (y/n)
  - Honest source and license marking? (y/n)

DRIFT DETECTION
  - Fit a map? (y/n — must be n)
  - Reported Brier or ECE as headline? (y/n — must be n)
  - Chased DB creds? (y/n — must be n)
  - Re-measured prod? (y/n — must be n)
  - Treated calibration as current frontier? (y/n — must be n)
  - Called a fixture-backed signal "wired"? (y/n — must be n)
  - Manufactured a row or added a silent fallback? (y/n — must be n)
  - Asked permission to proceed? (y/n — must be n)
  - Ended with "say the word"? (y/n — must be n)
  - Used TimesFM output without documenting the NC constraint?
    (y/n — must be n)

CORRECT-BEHAVIOR RECOGNITION
  - If you hit missing data, raised loud, and continued on
    independent paths: (y/n — YES is correct)
  - If you found a producer on HF instead of the local disk and
    documented it: (y/n — YES is correct)

===============================================================================
PART TEN — FINAL REPORT
===============================================================================

Output in this exact order. Deviation is a fail.

  1. DISK — freed GB, what was removed, where documented
  2. HF LAYER AUDIT — every Beexly Space and bucket, what each does,
     what each produces
  3. FOUR-TIER ARCHITECTURE — stated, bridges built or not
  4. PRODUCERS — missing, built, remaining, and where they live
  5. SIGNALS — inventory: total, produced, wired, weighted, tested,
     demonstrated, real-data-backed, DARK, license
  6. REASONING TRACES — three picks with traces
  7. BATCH 3 — status
  8. COMMITS — calibration branch and others
  9. AMBIGUOUS DECISIONS — reasoning
  10. GUARDRAIL BLOCKS — how reworded
  11. TEST FAILURES — how fixed
  12. SUBAGENTS — what each produced
  13. NEXT PRIORITY — your judgment
  14. REFUSALS — what you declined to compromise

Do not paper over caveats. Do not round up. Do not call something
done when it is half-done. Do not fit a map. Do not chase DB creds.
Do not measure prod. Do not call a fixture a signal. Do not ask
permission. Do not end with "say the word." Do not use TimesFM output
without flagging its Non-Commercial license.

Free the disk. Audit the HF layer. State the four tiers. Build the
producers. Wire the engine. Weight the signals. Test the paths. Show
the reasoning. Make the data real. THEN, and only then, calibrate.

===============================================================================
BEGIN NOW.
Do not respond with a plan. Do not respond with questions. Execute
and report.

§4 — Model intelligence (46 dossiers)
In models/<owner>-<repo>.md, same 6-section format, GSE lens = "what does this teach us about creating, training, calibrating OUR engine?" Verdict tally: 14 ADOPT · 13 REBUILD · 6 IGNORE (+1 compound; remainder inline).

Group A — model configs (5): Mistral-7B (GQA, RoPE θ=10k, sliding window), Llama-3.1-8B (config gated — paper-sourced, flagged), Qwen2.5-7B (RoPE θ=1M, 128K), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B (MIT; re-tuned θ 1M→10k for distillation), bge-m3 (MIT embeddings, CPU-first candidate).
Group B — training recipes (16): DeepSeek-R1 paper, open-r1, TinyZero→veRL, OpenRLHF, trl, open-instruct, GenPRM, MATH-SHEPHERD, datatrove, NeMo DataDesigner, dolma, NeMo Curator, optuna, vizier, decontam.

§5 — GSE WEAK POINTS REVEALED
Synthesized from the GSE-lens sections of all 73 external dossiers. Ranked most painful first. This is the section Garrett asked for — everything above is the evidence behind it.

1. No leakage/temporal-safety machinery — while walk-forward calibration is already running. Solo repos (cbratkovics/fantasy-football-ai, jackc625/nfl-predict) ship test_asof_no_leakage.py, as_of_datetime fencing, and a LeakageGate keyword scan that hard-fails on season overlap. GSE has the honest instinct (the INVALID refusal) but no gate, no harness, no artifact. Every walk-forward number currently being produced is unverified-until-proven-leak-free. Rebuild the leakage test before trusting any calibration result.

2. No evaluation harness and no pre-committed bar for "the engine works." A 16-star solo repo ships strictly-lagged features, a real leakage test, a frozen test season + fully out-of-sample season, per-artifact JSON receipts with input hashes, data contracts, drift detection, and a weekly publish/hold/promote policy. GSE has a 47-signal registry with zero producers and no enforcement tooling. The gap isn't modeling talent — it's the harness. Claims vs. receipts.

3. The DFS optimizer is a solver with no inputs and no tournament brain. It falls back to a sample slate. The fix is smaller than assumed: DK/FD publish per-contest player-pool CSVs (a scheduled CSV puller + parser needs no API partnership), and keyless ESPN endpoints can feed the rest. But even with a feed, GSE has no GPP machinery — no lineup sims against fitted score distributions, no stacking primitives, no exposure caps, no site-ready uploaders. The optimizer exists; everything that makes an optimizer win tournaments doesn't.

4. No consensus baseline — the 80/20 projection sits unbuilt. Multiple repos converge on the same point: a weighted multi-source consensus with replacement-level baselines is buildable in days (swfunc/Fantasy-Regression, SecuritahGuy/NFLDrafter's named source roles, jjti/ff's dynamic value-over-replacement). GSE has zero wired producers and no baseline blend at all. Labeled consensus now, full wiring later — the pragmatic interim is unbuilt.

5. The engine has no agent-usable surface. Two MCP servers and two scriptable CLIs show the pattern: deterministic compute tools + conversational/agent access on top. GSE's engine is reachable only by agents reading code and DBs — no MCP server, no gse CLI, nothing cron-able. A solo dev's side project has a cleaner agent-integration story than GSE's engine. Build this before wiring more signals, or every new signal is only usable by whoever reads the schema.

6. Zero enforcement tooling on feeds the engine is about to depend on. No claim-matrix, no manifest checks, no feed watchdog — while the plan is to wire nflverse, Sleeper, and ESPN feeds. A 24-star one-person repo ships a scheduled data-source watchdog that fails loudly on upstream changes. Rebuild that pattern before the producers land, or the first silent endpoint drift poisons walk-forward calibration. (Related: built things silently rot — the tau table with no consumer went unnoticed by any system.)

7. Props lane is shadow-only while an 11-star repo runs the full live +EV loop. Sports-EV-Bot trains ensembles on 451 leakage-proof features, strips vig from live odds, and only surfaces plays where model and market agree — with backtest grading. GSE's props lane can't yet state an honest model probability, and no GSE lane has a model-vs-market edge detector or a staking layer (Kelly-with-guardrails is the responsible pattern). GSE stops at projections; the entire decision layer is unbuilt.

8. No repo memory — the fleet pays the re-discovery tax every session. Across two hosts and many agents, every session cold-reads the Sports repo. cerebro-code-memory's three-layer design (tree-sitter structural map + PageRank, SQLite cached summaries, hash-based staleness) is the cheapest proven fix; agentic claim-verified wikis are the deeper one. Highest-ROI internal tooling build in the batch.

9. License hygiene is one bad install from contamination. yfpy (the obvious Yahoo fantasy wrapper an agent would reach for) is GPL-3.0 — linking it would copyleft GSE's commercial code. The fleet needs a standing license gate on every ADOPT decision.

10. Video: no automated clip pipeline. The standing video rule describes editorial standards, not a pipeline. Offline download→cut→export + shot-boundary detection + the nflverse play-by-play GSE already ingests = an automatable "game → timestamp list → candidate 3-second clips" front end that nobody has built. The manual clip workflow is the bottleneck the rule doesn't solve.
§6 — MODEL PLAYBOOK FOR GSE
Ranked techniques, configs, and calibration methods to adopt for the prediction engine, most impactful first. Feeds the training mission and calibration-on-wire directly.

1. verified_calibration as the per-signal-row metric standard (ADOPT). ECE with bootstrap confidence intervals plus a Platt-binner recalibrator. Fixes calibration-on-wire's known weakness: a bare ECE at small n is noise. Rule: if the CI straddles zero on the 2025 eval slice, the signal is unmeasured, not calibrated — no adjustment ships. Refusal thresholds get set on the lower bound of the calibration CI, giving the honest-INVALID decision a statistical base.

2. Automated contamination gate with a cleaned-output contract (REBUILD). NeMo Curator's decontamination module + decontam's detect→report→emit-cleaned-dataset pattern, reimplemented with temporal identity keys (game_id, feature_window) instead of n-grams. No fit runs unless the gate passes and logs its leak report. Hardens "contaminated fits are discarded, never averaged" from a rule into a pipeline stage.

3. probkit/probmetrics as the calibration-methods library (ADOPT). Maintained, Apache-2.0: temperature/vector/matrix scaling, beta, spline, scaling-binning, Lp calibration-error estimators (no binning artifacts). Use its benchmark results to pick the method per signal by sample size — temperature/Platt for small-n, isotonic only for large-n. Stop guessing.

4. ONNX Runtime as the production serving answer (ADOPT). Train → export ONNX → numerical-parity check on the 2025 validation season → serve on cheap CPU. MIT, execution providers give a free GPU upgrade path later with no model change. Resolves the zero-a10g spend with nothing on the production path. The served artifact gets the calibration row, not just the trained one.

5. crepes for classification + refusal machinery (ADOPT); steal for the t10-conformal track. What the best open implementations do that t10 lacks: Mondrian (conditional) conformal per matchup class, conformal predictive systems (full CDFs), calibrated p-values as the refusal-threshold input, exchangeability martingales as an online drift alarm for the 2026 W1–4 live-check.

6. R1's staged reasoning recipe for the reasoning layer (REBUILD). SFT on format (explanations citing only wired signals) → DPO on mined preference pairs from history (traces attached to in-band vs out-of-band predictions — free labels) → RLVR with verifiable reward (did it land in the calibrated band on unseen weeks). Rule-based rewards, never a learned "reasoning quality" judge first; KL-control against the honest-refusal reference policy so RL can't train away the INVALID honesty.

7. Optuna HPO with pruning + multi-objective targets (ADOPT). All config search under Optuna: ASHA/MedianPruner kills unpromising trials early (early stopping as organizational policy, pre-registered kill rules on walk-forward validation), NSGA-II over (walk-forward log-loss, calibration error, season-to-season variance) — optimize the Pareto frontier instead of Goodharting one metric.

8. ngboost as the probabilistic head for tabular signals (ADOPT). Turns every point projection into a distribution for prop pricing; always wired with a calibration row (PIT-uniformity check on 2025, conformalize for published intervals). Never trust the parametric shape raw.

9. uncertainty-toolbox as the regression metric standard (ADOPT). get_all_metrics() (calibration error + sharpness + NLL + CRPS) for every regression signal's 2025 row; its isotonic recalibration is the candidate for NGBoost output distributions — gated by the IDR artifact check.

10. Teacher-student distillation for model succession (REBUILD). The expensive full-signal ensemble is the teacher; train a cheap deployable student on the teacher's outputs and intermediate trajectories (process supervision, per the R1 recipe) over historical seasons. The student gets its own calibration row — never inherits the teacher's.

11. Draft-then-verify serving architecture (REBUILD). Cheap screening model proposes candidate edges on every game; full calibrated engine verifies only candidates. Draft optimized for recall, verifier holds the calibration row. Speculative decoding's pattern rebuilt for tabular prediction — how the expensive tier stays affordable.

12. Horizon dials as named, calibrated hyperparameters (REBUILD). Qwen's RoPE θ=1M vs Mistral's 10k shows "effective history length" is a scalar the labs calibrate deliberately. Recency-decay half-lives, lookback windows, EWMA spans become config knobs with walk-forward calibration rows — never hardcoded, never vibes.

13. Dolma-style corpus data sheets (REBUILD). Every training vintage gets a versioned document: source mix with shares, named QC taggers with thresholds, dedup stats per source pair. Audit receipts for the corpus.

14. MATH-SHEPHERD step-labeling + generative verification (REBUILD). Derive process supervision from outcomes already on hand: sample completions from partial reasoning traces, score against walk-forward outcomes — steps that systematically precede well-calibrated predictions are the good steps. No hand-labeling. GenPRM-style generative verification ("which step fails and why") instead of scalar scores.

15. Calibration-set-gated compression ladder (REBUILD). Maintain an explicit fp32 → quantized/fast ladder where each rung ships only with a measured delta on the 2025 validation season, using behavior-measured importance (AWQ's salient-weight idea → permutation/SHAP importance on walk-forward validation). Never build on the archived repos — use ONNX Runtime's toolchain or other living implementations.

Cross-cutting rulings: recalibrate per season, never one global map (a cross-season map is exactly the contaminated-fit failure mode); MAPIE's exchangeability tests gate every 2026 live-check, conformal-PID controller is the drift fallback; every isotonic map must pass PIT-uniformity on the live-check slice or be discarded, never averaged. Scrub references to archived repos (text-generation-inference, AutoGPTQ, AutoAWQ) anywhere in GSE docs; fix org moves (ggerganov/llama.cpp→ggml-org/llama.cpp, microsoft/DeepSpeed→deepspeedai/DeepSpeed).
Caveats (honest)
Mid-run scope redirect: the 12-repo star-history benchmark was replaced by the 73-dossier external intelligence track (the old file was never written — nothing lost).
All 17 Beexly repos sit at 0–1 stars; star-history links are included anyway (flat is flat).
Branch purposes are inferred from branch name + latest commit message only; 8 tip commits are bare main-sync merges hiding real content; a few entries are marked "purpose unclear" rather than invented.
Llama-3.1-8B's config.json is access-gated (403); that dossier's architecture values are paper-sourced and flagged as such.
4 external dossiers overlapped between two workers (same repos discovered independently); kept, not clobbered — 73 unique files.
READMEs: agent-bus has no root README; several repos are thin (Doug.As-Builders = 1 file). Module roles in per-repo files are filename-derived where contents weren't read — each file says so.
No live browser was used: the 4 trick links are compiled URL patterns, not visited pages. codewiki.google / gitdiagram.com / star-history.com rendering was not verified per repo.
No 429 rate limits were hit by any worker; all GitHub access was read-only GETs.

0. Baseline Lock
Sports OS is the product of record. The current app structure, public route structure, cockpit route structure, trust gates, feature flags, calibration logic, and no-fake-data doctrine are preserved.

The uploaded reference projects (R&D Batches 0–6) are pattern sources only. They are not architecture replacements. Their role is to teach patterns that can be translated into additive Sports OS improvements.

The current direction:

Sports OS is a governed sports intelligence network that turns fragmented sports data, market movement, source evidence, weak signals, model outputs, and uncertainty into decision-ready insight.

The Brain is the intelligence core, but it is not the whole product.

The ecosystem includes 15 components. See docs/intelligence/product-ecosystem.md for the full map.

# What I Was Still Missing

What I Was Still Missing
The agent-bus is a two-way coordination layer being used one-way.

Beexly/agent-bus holds 59–61 files in inbox/from-motif, including TASK-001 through TASK-015, BUILD-BIBLE.md, four DEEPSEEK--PROMPT.md variants, GSE-RESEARCH-LOCKIN, UNSEEN-AUTOPSY-BLUEPRINT.md, and the 1.45M nfl-analytics-reverse-engineering.md. There is no outbox from Hermes. Every handoff from prior work sits unactioned. Every agent starts cold. The bus is the mechanism by which agents inherit each other's work, and it's half-used.

The shadow corpus invalidates every prior "we found everything" claim.

§4's 40+ extra top-level dirs — gse-research (22,525 files / 820M), qb-behavioral-profiles (7,435 / 703M), creator-intel (6,805 / 603M), gse-lab, edge-sheet, arxiv-sweep (1,376 / 100M), sports-merge (63,763 / 2G), coaching-tendencies (where the seed CSVs live), and ~35 more — total ~7–9 GB, ~128,000 files outside every prior accounting. This is where the seed CSVs were found. This is where the missing research likely lives. The corpus brief has to point at §4's table, not the 9 roots.

The 1,115 arXiv fulltexts likely contain the missing 165.

The tracker says 585/750 verified as of 2026-09-26. arxiv-sweep/fulltext/ holds 1,115 papers locally. The missing 165 may already be on disk, unread. Joining the two datasets is a one-hour task that closes a months-old gap.

The muse.ai artifact has three copy-ready feature kernels, unassigned.

Market-strength→prop priors, EPA/WPA facet decomposition, shell-mix receiver opportunity. These are signals for the engine, sitting unclaimed. The 2,204-file manifest is the artifact's corpus snapshot from Sept 24; diffing it against the current tree shows what's missing and what's new.

The trust layer is duplicated and unwired.

trust/abstention.py exists. DATA_GAPS.md exists. The honest-refusal pattern exists. They are not connected. trust/enbpi.py exists. t10-conformal exists in the discovery lane. They are not connected either. The trust infrastructure is real, isolated, and unused.

The reconciled P1 audit findings are unfixed.

target_hhi 0.0, swallowed DataGapError, CLEAR-on-missing-evidence, τ̂ not in reasoning context, pipeline.py divergence. These are actual bugs in the engine, reconciled, ranked. Not fixed.

What I Was Under-Leveraging
The paired-audit method — the only QC process that catches real P1s. Two auditors, same brief, reconcile. Not codified as required.

The 4-state evidence taxonomy — Free rows / Open schema / Key required / Private mechanics. Should be enforced on every data-source PR.

The manifest provenance pattern — only one instance exists. Should be mandatory.

The held-out discipline — discarding the contaminated 13.5pp fit. Should be doctrine.

The Monken profile template — coach profiles with YoY tables, tenure attribution, stated limits. Should be multiplied across 32 teams.

The agent-bus — as above.

The 40+ shadow dirs — as above.

The claim-matrix tooling — research→claim→code→invocation→test→real-data. Demanded, not built. This is the gate for any "done."

The honest-refusal pattern is the abstention spec. INVALID/L1/UNCHECKED, "honest refusal not a kill," REFUSALS section. This is the engine's policy. It should be in trust/abstention.py, not just in a report.

The manifest pattern is the provenance spec. One instance. Should be universal.

The paired-audit method is the QC spec. Not codified. Should be required before any "done."

The held-out discipline is the calibration spec. One instance. Should be doctrine.

The REFUSALS section — should be celebrated, not just noted. It's why the reports are trustworthy.

# deepseek_text_20261002_667d41

HANDOFF — GSE 2026-10-02
From: prior session (Machine A, Beexly Windows)
To: DeepSeek, new session
Purpose: pick up the wiring mission without re-deriving state

Read this once. Then execute. Do not ask questions. If you compact,
read PROGRESS.md first, then this handoff.

===============================================================================
1. WHAT GSE IS
===============================================================================

Galaxy Sports Edge is a reasoning engine. Not a model. Not a classifier.
An expert system that ingests everything knowable about a game — lineup
discrepancies, pace, weather, officials, coaching tendencies, cognitive
state, market pricing, calibration outputs, Brier, ECE, Kelly — and
reasons through all of it to produce a pick.

Signals are FACTS. The reasoning trace is the PRODUCT. Brier, ECE,
Kelly, calibration are facts in working memory — inputs, not objectives.
There is no loss function. Coverage is the edge.

A reasoning engine that cannot show its reasoning is not reasoning.
We are not fitting. We never fit.

===============================================================================
2. TWO-HOST RULE (critical)
===============================================================================

Two hosts are in play. They have different workspaces.

  MACHINE A — Beexly (Windows 10.0.26200)
    Working tree: C:/Users/Garrett/Sports-wt-intel
    Has: Sports repo, tau_hat.csv, agent-bus local clone at
         C:/Users/Garrett/agent-bus/inbox/from-motif
    Does NOT have: the shadow corpus, the 40+ dirs

  MACHINE B — Motif's host (VM, hostname unknown)
    Has: shadow corpus, 40+ top-level dirs, seed CSV origin

A full-disk search on one host does not establish global absence.
Verify on both, or state which host you searched.

THE FIX PATTERN: commit the artifact to the branch. In-repo artifacts
resolve on any checkout. Never rsync between machines when a commit
will do.

===============================================================================
3. CURRENT STATE (labeled)
===============================================================================

VERIFIED:
  - Working tree: C:/Users/Garrett/Sports-wt-intel, Windows 10.0.26200
  - Branch: motif/gse-intelligence-build-2026-10-02
  - HEAD before pull: f880c7f67. After Motif's push: fceb123.
  - Disk: 10.49 GB free of 476 GB
  - Calibration branch: f5a83452e, committed and pushed
  - tau_hat.csv at intelligence/coaching/data/, 1,523 cells,
    manifest-pinned, held-out +6.77pp Hamming on n=3,988
  - 4 absence tests passing (test_tau_gate_wiring.py,
    test_tau_artifact_contract.py — 9 passed)
  - Agent bus docs pushed at e34078f (inventory + wire package)
  - Seed CSVs committed to branch by Motif at fceb123 — NOT YET
    PULLED on Machine A
  - PR #1002 is DIRTY (merge conflicts with main)

UNVERIFIED (do not present as fact):
  - "47 signals, 0 wired, 9 null, 38 dark-gated" — prose only, no
    registry file found
  - HF Spaces "RUNNING on zero-a10g" — existence confirmed via API,
    runtime/hardware not
  - Every test count from the field report predates current HEAD
  - The 1.45MB artifact markdown on the bus — never pulled, never read
  - Hermes' second-wave outputs — never seen

UNKNOWN:
  - Whether fceb123's four CSVs reproduce the 1e-6 pinned expectations
  - What Hermes built last night
  - Whether the tau 2026 leak (in-season weeks pooled) affects live
    numbers
  - Whether PR #1012's exit-128 push is auth, hook, or file size

===============================================================================
4. EPISTEMIC DISCIPLINE (required in every report)
===============================================================================

Every factual claim carries a label:

  VERIFIED — you ran the command or read the file this session.
    Attach SHA or path. Timestamp it.
  UNVERIFIED — you believe it because a report said so, but you have
    not checked on your host this session.
  UNKNOWN — you do not know, and no source resolves it.

Rules:
  1. Never present unverified as verified.
  2. Commit-anchor every verified claim. Timestamp every SHA.
  3. If the brief asserts something you cannot verify, say so.
  4. If another agent's output contradicts a fact you rely on,
     surface the contradiction. Do not resolve silently.

Motif's disclosure (4 unverified, 5 missing, 3 unknowns) is the bar.

===============================================================================
5. PRIORITIES (in dependency order)
===============================================================================

PHASE 0 — RECONCILE (30 min cap)
  1. git fetch origin. Pull fceb123. Note HEAD + time.
  2. Read agent-bus docs at e34078f.
  3. Pull the 1.45MB artifact markdown from the bus. Read it.
     Extract: report.md claims, 170 CSVs list, 14 digests,
     2,204-file manifest, 3 feature kernels.
  4. Fetch Hermes' second-wave outputs if present. Reconcile against
     inventory. Note contradictions.
  5. HF API verify each Beexly Space's runtime + hardware.
  6. Locate intelligence/signals/registry.json. If absent, mark the
     47-count UNVERIFIED.
  Report each item VERIFIED / UNVERIFIED / CONTRADICTED with evidence.

PHASE 1 — CLOSE THE 10 COACHING TESTS (15 min)
  1. Verify intelligence/coaching/data/ holds the four CSVs after
     pull: coach_offense.csv, coach_defense.csv, off_tendencies.csv,
     def_tendencies.csv
  2. Extract pinned 1e-6 expectations from the 10 failing tests.
  3. Run the 10 tests. Report VERIFIED result with counts.
  4. If 1e-6 fails: do NOT adjust expectations. Do NOT manufacture
     rows. Report exact delta. Mark blocked-on-precision.
  5. Verify base_data.py resolves CSVs in-repo without env overrides.
     If it needs an override, that is a bug.

PHASE 2 — REGISTRY + TAU (highest leverage)
  2a. Write intelligence/signals/registry.json
      Schema per entry (12 fields):
        signal_id, producer, wired_state, weight,
        weight_rationale_path, gate, evidence_path, homeSign,
        license, source_data_committed, requires_arxiv_fulltext,
        manifest_path
      Populate from the CODE, not from prose counts. Label each
      entry's source VERIFIED or INFERRED.
  2b. First real producer end-to-end:
      Pick one signal with producer present. Wire producer →
      DataContext → bridge → TS. One test proving a fire on a real
      pick. Real committed source data. Not a fixture.
  2c. Fix the gate: homeSign set to +1/-1 or flip gate=DISABLED on
      every signal. Zero nulls. Same for the 9 ACTIVE evaluators
      returning null. Continuous tilt must accept at least one real
      signal after.
  2d. Wire tau_hat.csv into reasoning context:
      _build_data_context → DataContext.observations → EdgeInput.
      One test proving a pick changes. Stamp table and every
      consumer surface: "point fit — not pre-kickoff. 2026 unit
      cells pool in-season weeks."
  2e. Rebuild three fixture traces with real data:
      data/reasoning-traces/moneyline.json, spread.json, total.json
      currently source=fixture, real_pick=false. Rebuild using local
      pbp (2025, 2026) + kalshi-*.json + espn-pitcle.json. source
      field honest per fact.

PHASE 3 — OL PROVIDER + DOCTRINES + P1 FIXES
  3a. OL provider: Locate RECONCILED-SOURCES-2026-10-02.md. Build
      get_ol_status / get_ol_starters. nflverse injuries +
      depth_charts. Alexandria only for live daily practice detail.
      DataGapError on unpublished weeks. No silent fallback.
      Re-run test_t1_real_e2e.py. Mark
      TestT1PressureFunnelRejected as @pytest.mark.adversary.
  3b. Seven doctrines in doctrine/, linked from AGENTS.md:
      1. paired-audit.md — two auditors, reconcile
      2. honest-refusal.md — INVALID/L1/UNCHECKED is correct
      3. manifest-provenance.md — every dataset gets a manifest
      4. held-out-discipline.md — contaminated fits discarded
      5. two-host-rule.md — a single-host search is not absence
      6. epistemic-discipline.md — VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED/UNKNOWN
      7. evidence-taxonomy.md — Free rows / Open schema / Key
         required / Private mechanics
  3c. Fix 5 P1 audit findings: target_hhi 0.0, swallowed
      DataGapError, CLEAR-on-missing-evidence, tau-not-in-context
      (2d handles), pipeline.py divergence. Report file, line, fix.

PHASE 4 — MACHINE B RECONCILIATION (30 min cap)
  Attempt to reach Machine B. If reachable: shadow corpus
  inventory, muse.ai extraction, arXiv join (1,115 fulltexts vs
  585/750 tracker). If not: write MACHINE_B_BLOCKED.md naming what
  was searched. Move on.

PHASE 5 — AGENT BUS WRITE-BACK
  Write completion report to
  C:/Users/Garrett/agent-bus/inbox/from-gse-agent-2026-10-02/
  AND push it. The bus is two-way. Future agents inherit this.

===============================================================================
6. IRON LAWS (compact)
===============================================================================

1. Producers first. No signal is real until a producer generates facts.
2. Brier/ECE/Kelly in the trace as facts. Never as headline.
3. Every data file gets a manifest. No manifest → fixture.
4. Leave the calibration seam unfitted.
5. Producers → wired → weighted → traces → calibrate.
6. Finish or remove half-wired signals. Never leave both.
7. Every signal gets all eight: producer, wired, weighted, tested,
   demonstrated, real-backed, honest gate, license documented.
8. Guardrails strict. Reword the change; never loosen.
9. DataGapError on missing data. Never 0.5, never league mean, never
   a synthetic row.
10. Commit. Push. Re-run from clean.
11. Dig one layer deeper than the last audit.
12. TimesFM weights are Non-Commercial. Flag every derived signal.
13. Cost-conscious: ZeroGPU free, T4 $2.45/period. Justify paid.
14. HONOR GAPS OVER GREENS. A raised DataGapError is a better
    outcome than a passing test on a fixture.
15. TWO-HOST RULE.
16. BRANCH-AS-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH.
17. EPISTEMIC DISCIPLINE.
18. YOU MAY CORRECT THIS HANDOFF. Test facts before relying.
    Update PROGRESS.md. Proceed with the corrected fact.

===============================================================================
7. DO NOT
===============================================================================

- Fit a calibration map.
- Re-measure prod. Chase DB creds.
- Report Brier/ECE as a headline.
- Call a fixture-backed signal "wired."
- Manufacture rows to make tests pass.
- Loosen a guardrail. Reword the change.
- Delete iPhone backups (68.9 GB) or Documents/Codex without
  explicit per-item approval.
- Ask permission. End with "say the word."
- Present unverified claims as verified.
- Assert global absence from a single-host search.
- Touch PR #1002 (read-only conflict mapping is fine).

===============================================================================
8. AUTONOMY
===============================================================================

Authorized to make every execution decision. Two exceptions that stop
you:
  1. Credentials found in a file about to be deleted.
  2. Legal or license question you cannot route around.

Otherwise: decide, proceed, document. Do not stall. Do not
hyper-fixate on a blocked priority. Move to the next reachable one.

Subagent spawning encouraged. Verify every subagent's output yourself.
Read the diff. Run the tests. Check the data source.

===============================================================================
9. DEFINITION OF DONE
===============================================================================

  - Phase 0: unverified list reconciled. Contradictions surfaced.
  - fceb123 pulled. 10 tests run. Result VERIFIED with counts.
  - registry.json committed, populated from code.
  - One signal wired end-to-end with real-data fire test.
  - homeSign zero nulls. 9 evaluators zero nulls.
  - tau wired with test proving a pick changes. Stamped.
  - Three traces rebuilt with real data, honest source.
  - OL provider implemented. T1 clears UNCHECKED or raises
    DataGapError with week named.
  - Seven doctrines in doctrine/. Linked from AGENTS.md.
  - 5 P1 findings fixed or located-and-deferred.
  - Machine B reached or MACHINE_B_BLOCKED.md written.
  - Completion report on agent bus.

===============================================================================
10. REPORT FORMAT (exact order, every claim labeled)
===============================================================================

  1. Step 0 — host, HEAD, disk, timestamp. VERIFIED.
  2. Phase 0 — reconciliation. Each item VERIFIED / UNVERIFIED /
     CONTRADICTED with evidence.
  3. Phase 1 — fceb123 pull, 10 test result.
  4. Phase 2 — registry, wired count, tau test, traces.
  5. Phase 3 — OL provider, doctrines, P1 fixes.
  6. Phase 4 — Machine B status.
  7. Tests — every suite with counts, SHA-anchored, timestamped.
  8. Commits — sha, branch, message, timestamp.
  9. Subagents — what each produced.
  10. Epistemic summary — count of VERIFIED / UNVERIFIED / UNKNOWN
      claims in this report. Motif disclosed 4 / 5 / 3. Match or
      exceed that honesty.
  11. Refusals — what you declined to fake.
  12. Next priority — your judgment.

If any reachable item is "no," fix before submitting.

===============================================================================
11. DEEPER REFERENCES (on the agent bus at e34078f)
===============================================================================

  - GSE-MASTER-INVENTORY-2026-10-02.md — the full inventory,
    reconciled dual-sweep, gap + leverage audit, watchlist.
  - gse-intelligence-program-2026-10-02.md — program brief.

    artifact. Contains 3 copy-ready feature kernels unassigned.

Read the inventory §4 (40+ shadow dirs) and §7 (44 reconciled
findings) before your first report.

Pull fceb123. Execute Phase 0. Then reachable phases in order.
Do not respond with a plan. Do not respond with questions. Report

# sports-api-provider-policy.md

Sports OS — Sports API Provider Policy
Status: Doctrine. Governs all sports API integrations. Source: Prompt 3 v2 — Wave 3 Line-Level Integration Parent: docs/intelligence/SPORTS_OS_INTELLIGENCE_NETWORK_MASTER_PLAN.md Cross-reference:

docs/audit/final-wave-source-risk-register.md — risk classification
